title: What's live and what's on a schedule
summary: Which numbers come straight from {pos} when you open a page, which are synced each night, and why.

blocks.text: Where {pos} lets RetailOps ask quickly, a page asks {pos} when you open it, with a short shared cache so many people opening it at once don't flood {pos}. Scheduled jobs still run as a safety net.

items: Today's Items Sold and Home's sales tile (shared for 1 minute; Refresh asks again).
Today's part of Open Checks (checked again when the last check is over 2 minutes old).
Suggested deliveries, Looks closed in {pos} and suggested schedules (worked out on request, and again after an upload or a confirm).

blocks.text: Live once an admin turns on Inventory from {pos}
On hand on Reorder Candidates, New order, Negative inventory and Refill from container uses {pos}'s count, at most 5 minutes old. See [Inventory from {pos}](article:setup-inventory-from-pos).

items: Past days of sales: synced each night, then compared with {pos} and corrected several times a day.
Barcode re-check against {pos}'s menu: every hour.
The nightly inventory snapshot from {pos}: 4:05 AM, when turned on.
The full Open Checks history sweep: once a day.
Phone alerts: at their set times, never between 10 PM and 7 AM.
Past days of sales come from the stored copy. Asking {pos} live would cost one request per day of the range.
{pos}'s own analytics run 2 to 4 hours behind, so they are only used for Insights and to check past days.
Deliveries received in {pos} show up with the next inventory upload.
Cost, vendor codes and last-received dates only come from an uploaded file.

blocks.text: Each page's ⓘ has a Where the numbers come from line with its own source and freshness.
